newsitem.title: USA: More rain forecast for US corn, soy growing areas.
newsitem.headline: More rain forecast for US corn, soy growing areas.

text.p: Rain should return to the U.S. Midwest Friday, after a short-lived respite Thursday, further delaying harvesting of corn and soybeans, meteorologists said.
"Everybody (in the U.S. Midwest) is going to get something but the rains should be heaviest in Iowa and the western Corn Belt," Craig Solberg of Weather Trades Inc said.
Solberg forecast showers late Friday and into the weekend should bring 0.10 to 0.40 inch of rain.
"It should be enough to slow down harvesting, especially as we had a real soaker earlier this week. It won't take a whole lot of rain to keep farmers out of the fields," he said.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis also said that the rains would return to the Corn Belt shortly.

"Harvesting has resumed across much of the western belt and will do so across the east during the day today (Thursday). Another storm will halt activity thru the weekend, and again at midweek," Davis wrote in a daily weather update.
"Good progress is getting hard to come by, and for the most part, an extended dry period does not appear to be on the horizon anytime soon," he added.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported Monday that the corn harvest was 30 percent complete as of Sunday, behind the five-year average of 46 percent.
The soybean harvest was 63 percent complete, also lagging the five-year average of 70 percent.

Solberg of Weather Trades, said another rain system should sweep across the Corn Belt late Tuesday and through Wednesday next week, bringing 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain. Heaviest precipitation should again be in the western Corn Belt.
He noted temperatures during the next week to 10 days would be cooler than normal in the western Corn Belt but near normal further east.
